transcript.text: The grill on my Hotpoint DD2540IX went bang with a bright flash and tripped the electrics. Reset the trip, oven works but grill is dead. There's a gap in the grill element. New element?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Please don't keep resetting the trip. Leave the oven switched off at its cooker switch (isolator) or at the fuse box and don't use it until it has been checked — never test it with the power on. One detail helps the engineer: does it trip as soon as it is switched on, or only after it has been heating for a while (or only on one function)?
It hasn't tripped again since I reset it, as long as I don't use the grill. It tripped straight away when the grill element flashed yesterday evening. I've left the grill alone since.

Thanks for letting us know about the tripping issue. Moisture is a common trigger for this problem. Please switch the oven off at the wall or its cooker switch (isolator) and let it cool completely first to ensure safety. Has the oven been cleaned recently with oven cleaner, steam or a lot of water, or got wet in any way?

No, it hasn't been cleaned with oven cleaner or steam and it hasn't got wet that I know of. The element itself has a visible break and a burnt blistered spot, so it looks like the element just failed. Is a new grill element the right fix?

[Heading: Element's insulation breaking down]
Thank you for letting me know it hasn’t been cleaned recently. Tripping once the oven has started heating, particularly on one function, usually points to an element whose insulation is breaking down. An appliance engineer needs to test this safely. Please keep it switched off at the cooker switch until then and don't keep resetting the trip. I'm not recommending a part from this.
